QUOTE: #ifndef MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS #define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) private_##member #else #define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) member #endif ... "the field is named `private_foo` for anyone who doesn't opt out" ... "so the library sees real member names everywhere" ... "external users don't get it by including the public headers"
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer explains both macro branches: opt-in code (library, programs) sees plain names, while ordinary consumers of the public headers see the `private_`-prefixed names.
